title: Read and write through git's streaming plumbing instead of one process per verb
description:
internal/runstate/git.go:152 commitWithFile writes every durable record as: hash-object, read-tree, update-index, write-tree, commit-tree, then push and rev-parse. Seven processes per record, ~90 records per fixture epic.

Measured: 21.6ms to spawn a git process on this machine; 0.90ms for the same query through a long-lived 'git cat-file --batch'. 24x, and process creation is the majority of a test's wall clock rather than git's work.

Git ships streaming plumbing for exactly this shape, and using it keeps full fidelity - it is still real git, the same on-disk format and the same ref semantics, so the defect classes this suite exists to catch stay catchable:
- git cat-file --batch for reads (one process, many queries)
- git hash-object --stdin-paths for blobs
- git update-index --index-info for index entries
- git fast-import where many objects or commits are written at once

Scope this tick to the read and object-write paths, held open per store instance. The commit/push batching is a separate tick because it changes what a record's durability means.
acceptance_criteria: The store reads and writes objects through long-lived batch processes rather than one process per operation. A counted run of the same reconcile end-to-end test spawns substantially fewer git processes (report the before and after counts). Every runstate and reconcile test still passes, and the FETCH_HEAD, refmap and peek-ref guards still fail when their regressions are reintroduced.
